sources.entry: Ebb - Open-source disk cleaner and AI-storage viewer for macOS, Windows and Linux that plans a cleanup you can read, moves removals to the Trash with a 90-day undo journal, and lets an MCP-capable AI client help without ever deleting on its own. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/ege-arhan/ebb) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: Ebb is an open-source disk cleaner and AI-storage viewer for macOS, Windows and Linux that plans cleanups for review, moves removals to the Trash with a 90-day undo journal, and lets MCP-capable AI assistants scan and plan without deleting anything.
keywords: share disk space with ai assistant
summary.what_it_does: Ebb scans a disk and shows where space is used, with a tide-style view of used versus safely reclaimable space. Cleanup is planned first: you review a plan, then apply it, and removed items go to the Trash with a journal that allows undo for 90 days. A Smart Clean screen gathers caches, old installers, idle project build folders and Trash into one plan. It also covers duplicate detection, type-aware compression, copy-on-write clones on APFS, Btrfs and XFS, large and old file finding, app uninstall with leftovers, startup items and a system health view. A CLI (ebb) exposes these commands with --json output, and ebb connect registers a local MCP server with several AI clients. The MCP tools can scan, explain and plan but have no apply or undo tool. Ebb also includes a local-model chat (ebb ask) that works through Ollama or LM Studio.
use_cases: find out what is filling up my disk
clean caches and old project build folders safely
uninstall a Mac or Windows app with its leftovers
see how much space AI tools and local models use
let an AI assistant inspect disk usage without deleting files
find duplicate or large forgotten files
notable: Plan, review, apply, undo workflow; nothing moves until a plan is confirmed and removals go to the Trash
MCP server with read and plan tools only; no apply or undo tool exposed to AI assistants
ebb connect configures Claude Code, Codex, Claude Desktop, LM Studio, Cursor, VS Code, Windsurf and Gemini CLI in one step
Copy-on-write clones for duplicate files and in-place compression for rarely opened folders
Cleanup recipes live in catalog/*.yaml so contributors can add new ones by PR
caveats: Apps are not code-signed yet; macOS and Windows show security warnings on first launch
Windows and Linux builds are verified by CI only, per the README
Some features depend on filesystem support (APFS, NTFS, Btrfs, XFS)
Optional once-a-day network check for new releases on GitHub (can be disabled)
